bug_semantics: Fluentd's in_http and in_forward inputs accepted attacker-controlled compressed payloads while enforcing limits only on the compressed bytes. Gzip, deflate, or zstd expansion was accumulated in memory without an uncompressed-size bound, so a small decompression bomb could exhaust process memory and deny service.
flaw_origin: The earliest released first-write of the advisory mechanism (inbound compressed payloads decompressed in memory with no uncompressed-size bound) is 335d3b2b709ad368da6655636e8ab401b116ae4b, the squash landing of PR #1179, which added CompressedMessagePackEventStream and in_forward gzip PackedForward handling. Immediate parent 657c85ff3f478150f10c0f90602af9ea905e5186 has no that receive path. Reconstructable PR member 74c0e0256dc020eb207d28dc0a459543167f1787 first wrote the in_forward wiring off-mainline. Commit 44186736165368c9839fb7958335bbf66ab2a6eb later added a second sink: in_http Content-Encoding with unbounded Zlib::GzipReader#read and Zlib::Inflate.inflate. Commit 30c3ce00ff165b1b5d9f53fc0a027074bbcab0da is a zstd/API expansion of the existing in_forward gzip path, not the in_forward introducer.
ai_marker: No AI marker on the earliest BIC object 335d3b2b709ad368da6655636e8ab401b116ae4b: author Yuta Iwama <ganmacs@gmail.com>, committer Satoshi "Moris" Tagomori <tagomoris@gmail.com>, 2016-09-13; reconstructable PR #1179 members are ganmacs-authored with no Co-authored-by/Generated-by/Assisted-by/bot trailers. The later in_http first-write 44186736165368c9839fb7958335bbf66ab2a6eb names Fujimoto Seiji as author and committer with only a matching Signed-off-by.
evidence: CVE-2026-44160 is PUBLISHED and describes unbounded decompression in in_http and in_forward, affected versions below 1.19.3, and the fix in 1.19.3; CNA references name f5f2b7cddf8aab3932e6dec9fa367a5f3eb27e10 and PR #5393. GHSA-j9cw-hwqf-85w7 withdrawn_at is null.

git log --reverse -S CompressedMessagePackEventStream -- lib/fluent/plugin/in_forward.rb starts at 335d3b2b709ad368da6655636e8ab401b116ae4b; parent 657c85ff3f478150f10c0f90602af9ea905e5186 still constructs MessagePackEventStream.new(entries) only. First tag containing it is v0.14.7; v0.14.6 does not contain it. v1.19.2 still contains the unbounded path.

44186736165368c9839fb7958335bbf66ab2a6eb is a one-parent public commit adding in_http Content-Encoding gzip/deflate whole-buffer decompression; parent 815e513bb9942f8846353700987249ea94c2b2f6 lacks that path. v1.2.2 does not contain it and v1.2.3 does. v1.19.2 blame of the GzipReader/Inflate lines still attributes them to this commit.

30c3ce00ff165b1b5d9f53fc0a027074bbcab0da is not the in_forward introducer: parent 29189a1c42a917ab672fb4561a2f51a3cdf74590 already has es_class = (option && option['compressed'] == 'gzip') ? Fluent::CompressedMessagePackEventStream : Fluent::MessagePackEventStream.

f5f2b7cddf8aab3932e6dec9fa367a5f3eb27e10 adds decompression_size_limit default 256 MiB and bounded chunked Extractor decompressors for in_http and in_forward. It is absent from v1.19.2 and contained in v1.19.3. Mainline 6c88e14e120316b9e83e29bc6d716b4313425004 has identical stable patch-id 4ae9f51710aafcd547c8f16781d784798295157d.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and patched, so FALSE_POSITIVE does not apply. The earliest released BIC is the 2016 in_forward compress feature squash 335d3b2b709ad368da6655636e8ab401b116ae4b, with parent proof the inbound gzip path was absent and reconstructable PR members that are also human-authored. The 2018 in_http Content-Encoding commit is a later independent first-write of a second sink, not the earliest BIC. The 2025 zstd commit is a surface expansion of the existing in_forward gzip path. Neither the 2016 BIC nor the 2018 in_http first-write carries an AI/bot/generator marker, so the causal authorship verdict remains NOT_AI.
